mediaItem.itemTitle: Wrongful Conviction Podcasts PSA - What to Do When Stopped by the Police (R
mediaItem.summaryNotes: This podcast segment is a public service announcement about legal rights during police interactions, hosted by Jason Flom of "Wrongful Conviction" and Robbie Atjawdhury of "Undisclosed."  The hosts discuss how to behave when pulled over by the police, emphasizing de-escalation and the importance of knowing and exercising one's rights.  Key advice includes stopping in a safe, well-lit area, remaining calm, keeping hands visible, and clearly stating the right to remain silent and to refuse searches. They promote awareness of legal rights to prevent negative outcomes during police stops and recommend an app called "Pulled Over by the Police" for recording interactions. The segment aims to empower individuals with knowledge of their rights to ensure safety and avoid unjust situations during police encounters.

keyQuotesRaw: Jason Flom & Robbie Atjawdhury: "We want to talk to you today about your rights and how they relate to interactions with the police."

Robbie Atjawdhury: "Remember you have the right to remain silent. You don't have to answer any questions at all. You can state loudly I have the right to remain silent and I am exercising my right. I will not answer any questions."

Robbie Atjawdhury: "You also don't have to consent to a search of your person or your belongings. And if you don't consent make sure they know it say I do not consent to a search of my person or my belongings."
Jason Flom: "Finally just remember this look if you're being arrested do not resist arrest. It does not end well."
